docs.title: vLLM Cluster Manager
docs.text:
Operate multi-node vLLM deployments

Spin up a host with a web dashboard, then add GPU nodes with the client agent. The UI lets you launch, monitor, and troubleshoot model deployments without building a full MLOps stack.

Best for
  • Research labs
  • Small teams
  • Multi-model serving
Built-in
  • Service discovery
  • Web UI
  • Systemd support

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Register and manage GPU nodes that run vLLM workloads.
  • Create model configurations and launch models on selected nodes.
  • Monitor node health and model status.
  • Stream logs from running processes for quick troubleshooting.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04
  • NVIDIA GPUs (H100, A100, L40, RTX 4090, DGX Spark)

Tip

New here? Start with the Getting Started guide, then review CLI Reference for flags and defaults.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
vLLM Cluster Manager runs three host services and a client agent on each GPU node.

Host services
  • Infra: Postgres + Consul via Docker Compose
  • Backend: FastAPI orchestration API
  • Frontend: React + Vite admin dashboard
Client agent
  • Python service that registers with Consul
  • Executes vLLM workloads on the node

docs.title: Service discovery
docs.text: Consul provides service discovery so the UI and backend can list connected clients.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. Client registers with Consul.
  2. Backend discovers clients and stores state in Postgres.
  3. UI calls the backend API and subscribes to WebSocket streams for logs and status.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Service Default Purpose Frontend 5173 Web UI (Vite dev server). Backend 8000 API + WebSockets. Consul 47528 Host port mapped to Consul HTTP API (container port 8500). Postgres 5757 Host port mapped to Postgres (container port 5432). Client 9000 Client agent HTTP server.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The CLI command is vllm-cluster-manager.

Run --help to see command and flag details: 

vllm-cluster-manager --help
vllm-cluster-manager host up --help
vllm-cluster-manager client up --help

docs.title: Host (host up)
docs.text: Flag Default Description --service false Run as a persistent systemd service. --host-ip 127.0.0.1 Bind host for the backend API and UI backend target. --host-frontend-port 5173 UI port. --host-discover-port 47528 Discovery port used by clients. --host-backend-port 8000 Backend API port. --postgres-host 127.0.0.1 Postgres host. --postgres-port 5757 Postgres port. --postgres-db vllm_admin Postgres database name. --postgres-user vllm Postgres user. --postgres-password change-me Postgres password.

docs.title: Client (client up)
docs.text: Flag Default Description --service false Run as a persistent systemd service. --host-ip 127.0.0.1 Host IP for discovery. --host-discover-port 47528 Host discovery port. --client-host 0.0.0.0 Client bind host. --client-port 9000 Client bind port. --node-name <hostname> Node name used for registration.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Launch host services in the foreground: 

vllm-cluster-manager host up --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-frontend-port 5173 --host-discover-port 47528

Launch a client node: 

vllm-cluster-manager client up --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-discover-port 47528 --node-name node-1

docs.title: Service mode
docs.text:
Service mode writes systemd unit files and enables them so they start automatically on boot: 

vllm-cluster-manager host up --service
vllm-cluster-manager client up --service

Warning

Service mode requires systemd and appropriate permissions. Use sudo when needed.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide takes you from a clean host to a working cluster with at least one client.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Host: - Docker + Docker Compose plugin (configure the docker group so no sudo is required) - Node.js + npm - Python 3.12 - uv (Python package manager)

Client: - NVIDIA GPU with CUDA - nvcc or nvidia-smi on PATH - Python 3.12 + python3.12-dev and build-essential (Debian/Ubuntu) - uv (Python package manager)

Install uv if you don't already have it: 

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

On Debian/Ubuntu: 

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3.12-dev build-essential

docs.title: Install (pip)
docs.text:
Create and activate a Python 3.12 virtual environment: 

uv venv --python=3.12
source .venv/bin/activate


uv pip install vllm-cluster-manager

docs.title: Start the host
docs.text:
Foreground (no sudo): 

vllm-cluster-manager host up --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-frontend-port 5173 --host-discover-port 47528

Persistent service (systemd): 

vllm-cluster-manager host up --service --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-frontend-port 5173 --host-discover-port 47528

--host-discover-port sets the discovery port used for clients. Use --host-backend-port to override the backend API port (default 8000).

docs.title: Start a client
docs.text:
Foreground (no sudo): 

vllm-cluster-manager client up --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-discover-port 47528

Persistent service (systemd): 

vllm-cluster-manager client up --service --host-ip 127.0.0.1 --host-discover-port 47528

Note

If the client cannot register, verify firewall rules and that the host is reachable from the client on the discovery port.

docs.title: Stop services
docs.text:
vllm-cluster-manager host down
vllm-cluster-manager client down

docs.title: Verify the UI
docs.text:
Open the UI at http://<host-ip>:<host-frontend-port>.

Common first-run checks: - The UI loads without a network error. - The host shows up as healthy. - The client appears under Nodes within ~30 seconds.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
The CLI writes service-specific env files under ~/.local/share/vllm_cluster_manager: - host/.env (Docker compose: Postgres + discovery service) - host/backend/.env (API service) - host/frontend/.env (UI) - client/.env (client agent)

If you edit any env file, restart the affected service.

docs.title: Firewall rules
docs.text: Allow these network paths (adjust ports to your flags): - User → Host UI: TCP host-frontend-port (default 5173) - UI/Browser → Host API: TCP host-backend-port (default 8000) - Clients → Host discovery port: TCP host-discover-port (default 47528) - Host → Client agents: TCP client-port (default 9000)

docs.title: Data persistence
docs.text: By default, shutting down the host (host down or stopping the systemd infra unit) runs docker compose down -v, which wipes the Postgres volume. Remove -v in code if you want to keep data.

docs.title: Service management
docs.text:
Systemd unit names (service mode): - vllm-cluster-infra.service - vllm-cluster-backend.service - vllm-cluster-frontend.service - vllm-cluster-client.service

Frontend behavior: - host up builds a static frontend bundle and serves it with the Vite preview server. - If you change frontend config or base path, rerun host up to rebuild.

Restart flows: 

sudo systemctl restart vllm-cluster-backend.service
sudo systemctl restart vllm-cluster-frontend.service
sudo systemctl restart vllm-cluster-client.service

docs.title: Host network setup
docs.text: If the host should be reachable from other machines, use a non-loopback --host-ip (for example the host's LAN IP) and ensure firewall rules allow inbound traffic.

docs.title: Reverse proxy base path
docs.text: If you proxy the frontend under a path like /vllm/, set VITE_BASE_PATH=/vllm/ in host/frontend/.env and restart the frontend service. This ensures asset URLs and API/WebSocket paths resolve correctly.

docs.title: GPU wheel selection
docs.text: The client bootstrapper detects CUDA from nvcc or nvidia-smi and installs a vLLM wheel that matches the detected version. If the wheel doesn't exist for your CUDA version, the install fails with a clear error.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This section captures the most common pitfalls and how to resolve them quickly.

docs.title: Client does not appear in the UI
docs.text:
Symptoms: Client starts, but no node shows up in the dashboard.

Checks: - Verify the client can reach the host on --host-discover-port. - Confirm the host is reachable from the client (use a non-loopback --host-ip). - Check firewall rules between client and host.

docs.title: UI loads but data is empty
docs.text:
Symptoms: UI opens, but no nodes or deployments show up.

Checks: - Ensure the backend is running on --host-backend-port. - Verify VITE_BACKEND_HOST in host/frontend/.env matches your host IP. - If you changed ports, restart the frontend service.

docs.title: Blank page behind reverse proxy
docs.text:
Symptoms: The UI shows a blank page when accessed through Nginx or another reverse proxy.

Checks: - If you proxy under a path (for example /vllm/), set VITE_BASE_PATH=/vllm/ in host/frontend/.env. - Restart the frontend service so Vite picks up the new base path.

docs.title: Consul port confusion
docs.text:
Symptoms: Clients fail to register when using the Consul default port (8500).

Explanation: - The host maps Consul's container port 8500 to a host port (default 47528). - Clients must use the host port (--host-discover-port, default 47528).

docs.title: CUDA detection fails
docs.text:
Symptoms: Client install fails with an error about CUDA detection.

Checks: - Ensure nvcc or nvidia-smi is on PATH. - Verify NVIDIA drivers are installed and the GPU is visible.

docs.title: vLLM wheel not found
docs.text:
Symptoms: Install fails after detecting CUDA.

Checks: - The vLLM wheel must exist for your CUDA version and CPU architecture. - If you are on an unusual CUDA version, consider installing a supported version or building vLLM from source.

docs.title: Data disappears after host down
docs.text:
Symptoms: Previously created deployments are gone after shutdown.

Explanation: - host down runs docker compose down -v, which wipes the Postgres volume. - Remove -v in code if you want persistent data.

Tip

When debugging, start the host in the foreground to see backend and frontend logs in the terminal.

docs.title: Documentation Versions
docs.text:
Use the version selector in the header to switch between releases.

How versions are published: - Tag a release like v0.1.2 and push the tag. - GitHub Actions builds and publishes that version. - The latest alias is updated to the most recent tag.

If you are viewing a non-latest version, consider switching to latest for current guidance.
